description: Agent-based diffusion-of-adoption model on a social network with peer influence, targeted policy broadcasting, contact scheduling, and adherence decay. Designed for calibration against daily adoption time series.

modules.name: ContactScheduler
modules.description: Generates daily contact events between persons based on a base small-world network, random mixing, and assortativity.

update_rule.pseudocode:
for each person i:
  base_neighbors = neighbors_of(i) in base_graph
  k_contacts ~ Poisson(contact_rate_mean)
  n_base = round(k_contacts * (1 - random_mixing_fraction))
  n_random = k_contacts - n_base
  contacts = sample_without_replacement(base_neighbors, min(n_base, len(base_neighbors)))
  # assortative random mixing by community and adoption
  candidate_pool = all_nodes if n_random > 0 else []
  if n_random > 0:
    weights = []
    for j in candidate_pool:
      w = 1.0
      if community_id(j) == community_id(i): w += assortativity_strength
      if adopted(j) == adopted(i): w += 0.5 * assortativity_strength
      weights.append(max(w, 0.001))
    contacts += weighted_sample_without_replacement(candidate_pool \ {i} \ base_neighbors, n_random, weights)
  for each contact j in contacts:
    w_ij ~ LogNormal(mu=log(edge_weight_mean^2 / sqrt(edge_weight_sd^2 + edge_weight_mean^2)), sigma=sqrt(log(1 + (edge_weight_sd^2 / edge_weight_mean^2))))
    emit (i, j, w_ij) into signal.contact_events
if Bernoulli(daily_rewiring_prob):
  rewire a small fraction of edges in base_graph using Watts-Strogatz with base_network_k and network_rewiring_prob
signal.contacts_per_capita_daily = len(signal.contact_events) / population_size
notes: Base network created at initialization via Watts-Strogatz (N, base_network_k, network_rewiring_prob).
Edge weights drawn lognormal to ensure positive contact strengths.
Assortativity increases likelihood of in-community and same-adoption-state contacts.

modules.name: PolicyBroadcast
modules.description: Selects influential targets and broadcasts policy messages that translate into person-level media exposure signals.

update_rule.pseudocode:
compute degree centrality deg[i] for all nodes i (cached)
K = max(1, floor(population_size * target_top_k_fraction))
targets = top_K_nodes_by(deg) excluding last_targeted_set if within retargeting_cooldown_days
if len(targets) > broadcaster_daily_budget:
  targets = random_sample(targets, broadcaster_daily_budget)
for each person i:
  baseline = 0.0
  if i in targets:
    baseline += message_intensity
  # spillover: neighbors of targets get partial exposure
  for neighbor t in neighbors_that_are_targets(i):
    baseline += 0.25 * message_intensity / max(1, degree(i))
  # apply media memory decay
  media_prev = media_memory[i] if exists else 0.0
  media_memory[i] = media_prev * (1 - media_decay_rate) + baseline
  signal.media_exposure[i] = media_memory[i]
signal.message_reach_rate = mean(1.0 if signal.media_exposure[i] > 0 else 0.0 for i in persons)
update last_targeted_set and last_targeted_day
notes: media_memory is per-person, decaying geometric memory of policy exposure.
Spillover models information diffusion beyond direct targets.

modules.name: AdoptionUpdate
modules.description: Updates person adoption and adherence based on peer influence through contact events, media exposure, personal thresholds, noise, and relapse dynamics.

update_rule.pseudocode:
initialize peer_influence[i] = 0 for all persons
for (i, j, w_ij) in signal.contact_events:
  peer_influence[i] += w_ij * adopted(j)
  peer_influence[j] += w_ij * adopted(i)
# cap influence by max_influence_neighbors and normalize
for each person i:
  peer_influence[i] = peer_influence[i] / (1.0 + max(1, min(degree(i), max_influence_neighbors)))
# compute adoption probability via logistic model
signal.adoption_transitions = []
for each person i:
  if not adopted(i):
    x = peer_influence_strength * peer_influence[i] + media_influence_strength * signal.media_exposure[i] + personal_bias(i) - adoption_threshold(i)
    p_adopt = 1.0 / (1.0 + exp(-(x)))
    p_adopt = clip(p_adopt + Normal(0, noise_scale), 0.0, 1.0)
    if Bernoulli(p_adopt):
      set adopted(i) = True
      adherence(i) = 1.0
      last_adopted_day(i) = current_day
      signal.adoption_transitions.append((i, 0, 1))
  else:
    # adherence decay and potential relapse
    adherence(i) = max(0.0, adherence(i) * (1 - adherence_decay_rate))
    if current_day - last_adopted_day(i) >= relapse_cooldown_days:
      if Bernoulli(relapse_prob * (1 - adherence(i))):
        set adopted(i) = False
        adherence(i) = 0.0
        signal.adoption_transitions.append((i, 1, 0))
notes: Logistic response to combined peer and media inputs against individual thresholds.
Adherence decay reduces commitment over time; relapse allows churn.

modules.name: ObservationAggregator
modules.description: Aggregates daily observables for calibration and evaluation.

update_rule.pseudocode:
adoption_rate = mean(1.0 if adopted(i) else 0.0 for i in persons)
new_adoptions = count of (i, 0, 1) in signal.adoption_transitions
contacts_per_capita = len(signal.contact_events) / population_size
message_reach = mean(1.0 if signal.media_exposure[i] > 0 else 0.0 for i in persons)
if smoothing_window_days > 1:
  apply moving average of window smoothing_window_days to each observable series
apply report_lag_days by shifting series forward if report_lag_days > 0
emit observables
notes: Moving average smoothing is optional and controlled by parameter.
Report lag can align model observables with reporting delays in data.

algorithms.NetworkGeneration: Watts-Strogatz small-world graph with N=population_size, k=base_network_k, p=network_rewiring_prob.
algorithms.ContactSampling: Poisson draws per agent with split between base neighbors and random mixing, weighted by assortativity; lognormal contact weights.
algorithms.PolicyTargeting: Degree-centrality top-k targeting with cooldown; geometric media memory with spillover.
algorithms.AdoptionDecision: Logistic function over peer and media inputs minus individual threshold with Gaussian noise; adherence decay and relapse.
algorithms.Smoothing: Simple moving average over observables with specified window.
